newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan says island landing was "illegal act".
newsitem.headline: Japan says island landing was "illegal act".

text.p: Japan's top government spokesman on Wednesday described a visit by a Japanese nationalist legislator to disputed islands in the East China Sea as an "illegal act".

But Chief Cabinet Secretary Seiroku Kajiyama told a news conference the islands were Japanese territory and there were no plans to prosecute the parliamentarian, who is a member of the main opposition group Shinshinto (the New Frontier Party).
China and Taiwan, which also claim the islands, reacted angrily to the landing on Tuesday by conservative politician Shingo Nishimura and three other other people.
The uninhabited islands -- known by Japan as the Senkaku Islands and by China as the Diaoyu -- lie 1,600 km (1,000 miles) southwest of Tokyo.

"The Japanese government has repeatedly stressed that the islands are territory under Japanese control, but in view of the landowner saying he does not want landings or other activities on the islands it was an illegal act," Kajiyama said.
